Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Scrambled-token chromatin priming time course
ideas.description: The material is a string of random 5–7 character tokens, each unique and order-independent. Treat each stimulus as a distinct token and expose cells to a transient stimulus (e.g., TPA, serum, or injury). Then use ATAC-seq and AP-1 (FOS/JUN) CUT&RUN over days to weeks to see whether AP-1-dependent accessible sites persist after the stimulus is gone. A second challenge then tests for faster or stronger transcription at those sites.

ideas.title: Combinatorial dimer-code perturbation
ideas.description: The material resembles a code built from many different token combinations, so the idea is that AP-1 memory may be encoded in which FOS/JUN/ATF dimers form, not just in total AP-1 activity. Use dimer-specific CUT&RUN or ChIP-seq, plus targeted degradation of individual members (dTAG), to find which compositions at which enhancers are needed to maintain primed states.

ideas.title: Single-cell lineage-barcoded heterogeneity test
ideas.description: Each token is unique, like a cell barcode. Label clonal lineages with barcodes, stimulate transiently, and use single-cell multiome (RNA plus ATAC) to ask whether sister cells share AP-1 motif accessibility and response strength after division more than random cells do. Shared states would indicate heritable memory.

ideas.title: Acute AP-1 degradation after priming
ideas.description: Prime cells, then remove AP-1 (inducible degron or dominant-negative A-FOS) after the stimulus ends and before re-challenge. If memory needs continuous AP-1, the primed accessibility and enhanced response should decay. If AP-1 only initiates memory, they should persist. This separates initiation from maintenance.

ideas.title: Synthetic AP-1 reporter with live imaging
ideas.description: Build a reporter with AP-1 motifs in varied arrangements and spacings, like arranging tokens in different sequences. Image single cells over multiple stimulus pulses with varied intervals to quantify hysteresis, pulse-history dependence, and decay time. Mutating motifs or adding methylation inhibitors tests which sequence features and chromatin marks carry the memory.
